title: Work done by gravity
brief: A body is carried along a path in N small steps and the work W = Σ F·ds is summed step by step, shown live next to the value predicted from the end points alone. Preset 'uniform': uniform downward gravity (mg = 1 per length unit); two paths A (curved) and B (straight) from point 1 to point 2 are traversed together; both totals equal mg(z1 − z2). With the stepped toggle each step becomes a vertical then a horizontal leg; only the vertical legs do work. Preset 'central': a closed loop near a point mass M with F = GMm/r² toward M; the expected value is GMm(1/r − 1/r1); the stepped toggle replaces each chord by a radial leg and a circular arc, the arcs doing no work, so the total around the loop returns to zero.

beats.caption: Uniform gravity points straight down, so only the vertical part of each step does work. Paths A and B end with the same total, $mg(z_1 - z_2)$.
Break each path into vertical and horizontal steps. The horizontal steps add nothing; the vertical ones add up to the drop.
Around a central mass, a smooth loop can be followed by radial and circular steps. The circular steps do no work and the radial ones cancel, so the loop totals zero.
With finer steps the stepped path hugs the smooth loop, and the total still comes back to zero.
